name: Eiji Miyazaki

tenures.source: Won the opening bout of the promotion's own debut card by referee stoppage, then stood in the entranceway during a later bout on the same card, rumoured to have been sent by a rival promotion to scout its own newest signing. Fought to a double disqualification in a World Heavyweight Championship tournament quarter-final at the promotion's own second event, eliminating both men from that bracket slot.

caption: Opened the promotion's own debut card with a referee-stoppage win, then loomed in the entranceway during a rival's debut, rumoured to be scouting him for another promotion.

name: Reyo Ruas

tenures.source: Lost the opening bout of the promotion's own debut card by referee stoppage.

caption: Lost the opening bout of the promotion's own debut card by referee stoppage after absorbing a series of strikes.

name: Marco Russ

tenures.source: Lost the debut card's own second bout to a cross armbreaker, a rematch of an earlier, unrelated shoot-fighting draw between the two men. Lost a special bonus bout by heel hook submission at the promotion's own second event.

caption: Lost by submission on the promotion's own debut card in a rematch of an earlier real-world shoot-fighting draw against the same opponent.

name: Minoru Hidaki

tenures.source: Lost the debut card's own third bout to a dragon suplex in just over two minutes.

caption: Lost the promotion's own debut card in just over two minutes to a released dragon suplex.

name: Sunjinski

tenures.source: Won the debut card's own fourth bout by pinfall with his own signature suplex, marking his first Japanese-ring appearance since an earlier promotion's heavyweight division had closed. Lost a World Heavyweight Championship tournament quarter-final by submission at the promotion's own second event, his own shoulder injury worked throughout the bout.

caption: Marked his first Japanese-ring appearance in some time with a pinfall win on the promotion's own debut card, once the only heavyweight champion of a promotion that had since closed.

name: Takao Yoshie

tenures.source: A former judo champion returning from injury, lost the debut card's own fourth bout by pinfall.

caption: A former judo champion whose return from injury on the promotion's own debut card ended in a pinfall loss.

name: Shiro Mayashi

tenures.source: Won the debut card's own fifth bout by rolling armbar after a hard-fought exchange, then publicly complained his own billing undersold the match. Lost a nineteen-minute World Heavyweight Championship tournament quarter-final by submission in overtime at the promotion's own second event.

caption: Won a hard-fought submission on the promotion's own debut card, then publicly complained that his billing on the card undersold the fight.

name: Alexandar Karloff

tenures.source: Billed as a veteran fighter with a record 60-minute draw on his own resume, lost the debut card's own fifth bout by submission. Won a special bonus bout by heel hook submission at the promotion's own second event, added to replace a cancelled tournament slot.

caption: A veteran fighter billed on the strength of a legendary 60-minute draw, submitted on the promotion's own debut card.

name: Junji Shirow

tenures.source: Billed by the promotion's own television campaign as a future star, won the debut card's own sixth bout by armbar submission. Won a nineteen-minute World Heavyweight Championship tournament quarter-final by submission in overtime at the promotion's own second event, then lost a semi-final by submission.

caption: Billed by the promotion's own television campaign as a future star, won the debut card's own sixth bout by armbar submission.

name: Kazuo Iizuka

tenures.source: Lost the debut card's own sixth bout by armbar submission.

caption: Outmatched from the opening bell, submitted on the promotion's own debut card.

name: Keiji Asamiya

tenures.source: Won the debut card's own main event by disqualification against a longtime rival, continuing a rivalry the card's own coverage traces through five earlier bouts. Won the promotion's own second event's opening quarter-final by submission, then advanced to the World Heavyweight Championship tournament final on a bye after a rival bout ended in a double disqualification, losing the title match itself to a referee stoppage over an arm injury.

caption: Won the promotion's own debut main event by disqualification, the sixth chapter in a rivalry that had already produced two wins apiece and a riot-ending draw.

identity.note: A different fighter of the same name is recorded elsewhere in the held record, at an unrelated promotion; this promotion's own card gives its own man a separate rivalry history and a specific earlier bout dated July 1997, matching nothing in the other record.

name: Takashi Fukada

tenures.source: Lost the debut card's own main event by disqualification after a low blow, then won the promotion's own first World Heavyweight Championship at its second event and still held it as of the promotion's own year-end ranking report. At the second event itself, won a quarter-final and a semi-final by submission before winning the tournament final on a referee stoppage over his opponent's arm injury.

caption: Lost the promotion's own debut main event by disqualification, then won its first World Heavyweight Championship at its second event and was still champion at year's end.

name: Hadi Moditian

tenures.source: The promotion's own owner and producer, self-announced at its founding press conference and billed opening its debut card before a sellout crowd. Addressed the crowd again at the promotion's own second event, presented the new champion with the title belt, and briefly halted the tournament final over a fighter's arm injury.

caption: The promotion's own owner and producer, a former wrestling announcer who founded the promotion after the earlier one he headed closed under debt.

name: Tajiri Hayashi

tenures.source: The promotion's own head official, a ten-year veteran referee billed in its rules document and presiding over its debut card. Presided over the promotion's own second event, including its tournament final's referee stoppage.

caption: The promotion's own head official, a veteran referee who laid out its fighting rules before presiding over its debut card.

name: Kunihiro Yamamoto

tenures.source: Billed in the promotion's own rules document as its color commentator, credited by the fictional nickname "Father of Strong Style."

caption: Billed by the promotion as its color commentator and, in its own words, the "Father of Strong Style."

name: Kyoko Kosugi

tenures.source: Billed in the promotion's own rules document as its press director and in-ring interviewer, a former magazine journalist.

caption: Billed by the promotion as its press director and in-ring interviewer, a former wrestling magazine journalist.

name: Chandrasekhar Yoshida

tenures.source: Debuted with an extended promo renouncing the bushido traditions of two other already-held promotions, then fought the promotion's own first Super-Middleweight exhibition to a time-limit draw.

caption: Debuted with a bitter renunciation of the bushido codes of two other already-held promotions, then fought the promotion's own first Super-Middleweight bout to a draw.

name: John Taylor

tenures.source: Made his Japanese debut in the promotion's own first Super-Middleweight exhibition, fought to a time-limit draw.

caption: Made his Japanese debut in the promotion's own first Super-Middleweight bout, fought to a time-limit draw.

name: Kiato Toyota

tenures.source: Billed as the promotion's own ring announcer, calling official decisions at its second event.

caption: The promotion's own ring announcer, calling official decisions at its second event.
